Tax Codes

Assign reporting categories to reverse-charged tax codes to organize net amounts in reports and tax returns.

These categories specifically handle transactions where the tax liability is transferred from the supplier to the recipient.

Name
Name

Reporting categories for reverse-charged tax codes are classification labels used to organize net amounts for transactions subject to reverse charge mechanisms.

Reverse charge applies when the recipient of goods or services, rather than the supplier, accounts for the tax. This commonly occurs with cross-border services, construction services, or specific commodity trades.

Common Reporting Categories

The following categories are commonly used for reverse-charged net amounts:

• Intra-community acquisitions - For goods purchased from other EU member states

• Imported services - For services received from foreign suppliers

• Construction services - For subcontracted construction work (domestic reverse charge)

• Mobile phones and electronics - For wholesale trades subject to reverse charge

• Scrap metal and waste - For trades in recyclable materials

• Energy and emissions - For gas, electricity, and emission allowances

• Cross-border B2B services - For business services from foreign providers

Benefits

Using reporting categories for reverse-charged transactions provides:

• Proper segregation of reverse charge transactions from standard transactions

• Accurate reporting of both output tax liability and input tax deduction

• Compliance with specific reverse charge reporting requirements

• Clear audit trail for tax authorities reviewing reverse charge application

• Prevention of tax reporting errors through systematic categorization

Set up categories that match your local tax authority's reporting requirements to ensure compliance and accurate tax filing.
